scope: Retrospective provenance backfill from repository reports plus N56/N57 publisher audit. Original data never copied; not systematic or claim of accessing raw data for bibliography.

sources.title: Gale y Shapley (1962), College Admissions and the Stability of Marriage
sources.contribution: Modelo de matching estable; ordenamientos comunes pueden generar emparejamientos por rango sin utilidad por semejanza
sources.limits: Teoría formal bajo hipótesis de estabilidad; no observa aplicaciones reales

sources.title: Hitsch, Hortaçsu y Ariely (2010), Matching and Sorting in Online Dating
sources.contribution: Antecedente fuerte de preferencias y matching estable para explicar sorting en plataforma; Auditoría post hoc 2026-10-28: fuente primaria AER 2010 Tabla 4 (p.149) distingue perfiles visitados (hombres 385470, mujeres 172946), primeros e-mails (49223/14178), y primeros contactos que llegan a 'match' definido como intercambio de información de contacto (2130/914); el artículo declara que se observaron registros de browse/contact por usuario. Precedente fuerte de modelado de etapas.
sources.limits: No se han reanalizado sus datos originales; no prueba caída de estatus por rechazo; no trasladar ratios de usuarios que navegaron a simulación ESBM de impresiones ofrecidas por algoritmo, ni interpretar 'match' de contacto como relación estable o reciprocidad de swipe. La tabla es publicada, NO reestimada.

sources.title: Bruch y Newman (2018), Aspirational Pursuit of Mates in Online Dating Markets
sources.contribution: Demuestra aspiración jerárquica en iniciación de contactos; constriñe originalidad de aspiración
sources.limits: Aspiración observada no equivale a reciprocidad estable o pérdida de prestigio

sources.title: Choo y Siow (2006), Who Marries Whom and Why
sources.contribution: Economía estructural de matching y matrimonios; antecedente de emparejamiento agregado
sources.limits: Matrimonio no equivale a interés en aplicación; no se procesó su base

sources.title: INE, Estadística Continua de Población 2026
sources.contribution: Total demográfico de España y sexo, pero no denominador de usuarios activos disponibles
sources.limits: No se recuperó tabla nacional 20–39 sexo ni elegibilidad sentimental

sources.title: INE, Encuesta de Condiciones de Vida 2025
sources.contribution: Ancla renta material española; permite diseñar segmentación socioeconómica
sources.limits: Renta no es reputación romántica ni atractivo; no hay microdatos usados

sources.title: Jessica Fong (2024), Effects of Market Size and Competition in Two-Sided Markets: Evidence from Online Dating
sources.contribution: Randomized user-level information about local opposite-side market size and same-side competition in platform; larger market signals depress participation, conditional selectivity increases with market and decreases with competition.
sources.limits: Information treatment, not exact observed encounter counts nor a universal size effect. Raw person-level data not downloaded; field experiment abstract read.
sources.precise_note: Source discovery before present synthetic computation; results have not been used as training data for this model

sources.title: Junwen M. Hu and David M. Markowitz (2026), Re-examining relational pursuit and mate selection in online dating
sources.contribution: Two preregistered experiments (n=193,342), 31 vs 6 hypothetical choice options, greater reported pursuit with more options, partly mediated by perceived compatibility; supports separating information, compatibility, cognitive load.
sources.limits: Participants select from experimental profiles, not genuine reciprocal platform decisions or long-term couple formation. OSF data cited but files not retrieved.
sources.precise_note: Source discovery before present synthetic computation; results have not been used as training data for this model

sources.title: Büyükeren, Makarin and Xiong (2026), The Impact of Dating Apps on Young Adults: Evidence from Tinder
sources.contribution: Causal-style difference-in-differences on launch diffusion within US colleges; more sexual activity but little movement in long-term relationship formation/quality; inequality rose in some outcomes, especially men.
sources.limits: Not a randomized Tinder platform intervention or same as speed dating. NCHA survey and replication package referenced; no raw AEA replication file inspected. Social harms require context not inferred from toy.
sources.precise_note: Source discovery before present synthetic computation; results have not been used as training data for this model

sources.title: Soohyung Lee and Muriel Niederle (2025), Propose with a rose? Signaling in internet dating markets
sources.contribution: Field experiment randomizing endowment of two versus eight virtual roses as signals of interest, isolating a priority-signal mechanism apart from attractiveness rankings.
sources.limits: Abstract only, no participant-level dataset; did not reproduce effect sizes or model significance. A rose is a signal, not reputation decline.
sources.precise_note: Source discovery before present synthetic computation; results have not been used as training data for this model

sources.title: Sunmi Jung and Lester Lusher (2026), Dating apps and marriage rates
sources.contribution: Event-study/difference-in-differences with CPS and Tinder Google-search intensity finds no overall marriage-rate effect and association with higher separation/divorce, especially thin markets.
sources.limits: Search intensity proxy for exposure and observational identification assumptions; access to participant microdata/replication not available, so does not calibrate synthetic breakup hazard.
sources.precise_note: Source discovery before present synthetic computation; results have not been used as training data for this model

sources.title: OpenICPSR / AEA replication record for Büyükeren et al. (2026)
sources.contribution: AEA/RePEc identifies replication package for new 2026 Tinder paper; possible external data and code to inspect with appropriate download and rights checks.; 28/10/2026 official repository V1 exposed four directory names plus 256.1KB README.pdf, with >1.1M student survey responses 2008–19 and individual/college-level DID analysis. Read archive landing metadata only.
sources.limits: Link from RePEc verified, but web resolver inaccessible; direct aeaweb materials ZIP download failed, no files, code, microdata, license or columns inspected; NOT an independent replication.; inner files, README bytes and dataset-specific LICENSE still unavailable due web cache and container DNS. No candidate-level impressions/reciprocal decisions documented. ICPSR in 2026 migrating openICPSR; DOI still expected to redirect but unsuccessful here.
sources.precise_note: Source discovery before present synthetic computation; results have not been used as training data for this model
sources.latest_access_recheck: 2026-10-28: web click README and Data returned HTTP403, full project download redirects to ICPSR authentication. No bypass; no retrieved README/data.

sources.title: Rosenfeld, Thomas, Hausen (2023) HCMST 2017/2020/2022 combined public dataset, Stanford Libraries
sources.contribution: Independent longitudinal cohort 3510 participants baseline 2017, 2107 follow-up 2020, 1722 follow-up 2022; online dating channel, partner/couple formation context and relationship outcomes. Includes LGB oversample and weights. Core potential external data for relationship persistence rather than dyadic swipe choice.; Stanford ficha original especifica 2862 con pareja vigente y 541 sin pareja actual pero con pareja anterior que contestan batería relacional; instrumento no se restringe por completo a quienes tienen pareja vigente.
sources.limits: Not a profile-exposure log and no prospective popularity, declined candidates or bilateral directed decisions; official Stata/SPSS/RData/codebook announced but bytes not downloaded. Longitudinal attrition and baseline partner selection; Stanford data-use terms impose nonidentification, noncommercial redistribution, author notification and citation.; subgrupos del cuestionario no representan 3403 parejas observadas ni episodios completos; no se han comprobado microdatos/codificaciones.
sources.latest_metadata_recheck: 2026-10-28 Stanford source webpage and ICPSR version record reviewed; Stata and codebook file requests returned HTTP403; no row bytes

sources.title: ICPSR 38873.v1 (2024), HCMST 2017/2020/2022 archival catalog and study methodology
sources.contribution: Confirms survey unit individual, original release 2024-02-07, same Stanford 3510/2107/1722 sample, LGB oversampling, analytic and attrition weights, timing and relationship questions; verifies it is panel data, not independent third sample.
sources.limits: Same underlying cohort as SRC048, so NOT independent evidence. Institutional ICPSR member access terms may differ from Stanford public download. File/coded variables not inspected in this execution.

sources.title: ICPSR 2026, openICPSR transition FAQ and maintained DOI routing
sources.contribution: Official announcement that repository interfaces and deposits are being migrated and DOI persistent redirects preserved, clarifying that old openICPSR links may not be canonical entrypoints.
sources.limits: Does not prove any particular E218862 URL failed because of migration, nor prove restricted vs public-use access to its files; requires direct license check.

sources.title: German Family Panel pairfam, GESIS archive study ZA5678, Release 14.2
sources.contribution: Independent German longitudinal cohort, 14 annual waves 2008–2022, with primary respondents and selected partner respondents, longitudinal prospective/retrospective relationship/cohabitation/marriage episodes; linked respondents and partner reports. Distinct measurement class versus HCMST one-sided survey.
sources.limits: SUF not acquired or processed; only registered users via GESIS; no full exposure/initiations/rejections or choice-set observations. Recalled partner episodes and selective current-partner interviews, left truncation, attrition. Same source as SRC052 manual, not a second independent cohort.

sources.title: Brüderl et al. (2024), pairfam Data Manual, Release 14.2, LMU/GESIS
sources.contribution: Primary technical PDF visually inspected: biopart month-level episodes and partner survey merge by id; notes that 14.0–14.2 biopart does not incorporate wave14; anchor-only relationships, missing/imputed dates and right-censoring, partner sample weights not constructed.
sources.limits: Codebook and SUF variable distribution/data rows not processed; manual is documentation for SAME pairfam source as SRC051, not independent empirical replication. Partner participants only selected and current partners.

sources.title: AEA/ICPSR archive E112322V1 (2019), replication data for Hitsch, Hortaçsu and Ariely 2010
sources.contribution: Official replication package directly linked from AEA article has folder 20080317_data and LICENSE.txt. Source class potentially contains data/code for 2010 online browsing->email->contact-exchange stages, unlike survey outcome-only archives. Need inspect actual folder, README, rights and individual fields; nothing inside package recovered.
sources.limits: No ZIP, inner file names, LICENSE text or datasets obtained; ICPSR folder and license clicks cache miss. Do not equate listed folder with raw browser histories or claim data analysis. E112322V1 is the canonical AEA publisher link; similarly titled dev mirror E108424 is NOT counted independent and should not replace AEA citation.
